title: Electron-phonon control of obstructed and quantum spin Hall topology in an altermagnet
authors: Kuntal Bhattacharyya, Bilal Tanatar, Saurabh Basu
abstract: We theoretically demonstrate control over the interplay between obstructed atomic insulating and first-order topological phases via electron-phonon coupling (EPC) in a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) that hosts nonrelativistic spin-split bands with zero net magnetization. By embedding a $d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$-wave AM in a quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulator, we show that an altermagnetic order beyond a critical strength reconstructs the parent QSH state of a Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ)-type topological insulator (TI) into an obstructed atomic insulator (OAI), characterized by nontrivial bulk polarization with quantized fractional corner charges, accompanied by characteristic in-gap boundary states, while the spin Chern number vanishes. Upon incorporating sufficiently strong EPC, the polaronic dressing reorganizes the Wannier centers and the associated effective edge topology, thereby weakening the altermagnetism-induced OAI phase and restoring the helical QSH edge modes. Further, EPC eventually drives the system into a trivial insulator. By uncovering a controllable switching mechanism between topologically distinct insulating phases in AMs, our study establishes a direct route toward phonon-tuned spintronic functionalities in unconventional magnetic platforms.
summary: This theoretical study demonstrates that electron-phonon coupling (EPC) can act as a switch to control topological phases in altermagnets. By tuning the EPC strength, the system can transition from an Obstructed Atomic Insulator (OAI) back into a Quantum Spin Hall (QSH) state, offering a phonon-mediated route for spintronic device functionality.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate controllable switching between distinct topological insulating phases (OAI, QSH, trivial) in an altermagnet by tuning the electron-phonon coupling (EPC).
main_result: EPC can weaken the altermagnetism-induced Obstructed Atomic Insulator (OAI) phase, thereby restoring the helical Quantum Spin Hall (QSH) edge modes, establishing a phonon-tuned spintronic control mechanism.
method: The authors employ theoretical modeling using effective Hamiltonians derived from the BHZ model, incorporating the Holstein EPC term via the Lang-Firsov transformation.
model_or_system: The system is a d-wave altermagnet embedded in a QSH insulator, modeled using a 4x4 BHZ TI Hamiltonian. The analysis tracks the evolution of topological invariants and edge states as the altermagnetic strength ($\Delta_{AM}$) and EPC strength ($g$) are varied.
key_observables: Spin Chern number ($C_s$), total Chern number ($C_{	ext{tot}}$), bulk polarization ($\mathbf{p}$), quantized fractional corner charges ($Q_{	ext{cor}}$), and the presence/nature of edge states (helical vs. suspended).
important_parameters: Altermagnetic strength ($\Delta_{AM}$), EPC coupling strength ($g$), and critical transition points ($\Delta_{	ext{AM}}^c$, $g_{c1}$, $g_{c2}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Lang-Firsov transformation and projecting the system onto the zero-phonon sector, treating the system in the high-frequency anti-adiabatic limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of bulk and edge spectra across phase transitions, showing gap closing at critical $\Delta_{AM}$ values and the restoration of helical edge modes upon EPC inclusion.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the topological phases (QSH $	o$ OAI $	o$ Trivial) as $\Delta_{AM}$ increases, then incorporates EPC to show how the system transitions back through a QSH-like state before becoming trivial.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical framework for realizing tunable topological spintronics using lattice vibrations (phonons), which is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in solid-state materials.
